translation:
How about you stand up before you start
grumbling about this and that?
R-right.

Well, did you end up finding the man-eating
classroom?
Well, that's…
There's no way I can tell her the truth.

On the other hand, it doesn't look like Haruhi
will be satisfied with nothing…
Hello? How did it go?
Ah, unfortunately we got nothing.
What…?

You could plainly see her complexion
changing…

Us as well. We carried out the most thorough
investigation we could, but…

Unfortunately, there were few clues to be
found.

Rather, it's highly unlikely that there were
any clues for us to find in the first place.
What do you mean by that, Koizumi?

For example, what if this was a mere mistake
or misunderstanding?

To begin with, there's only a single person who
claimed to have seen class 1-10.
The Computer Research Society member, huh.

Indeed. We're not in a comfortable position to
disprove…

…that the event occurred only within his
head, don't you think?
What are you trying to say exactly?
If he were confused or misguided…

…it wouldn't be surprising that no trace of
evidence was left behind to find.

That's certainly a sound argument, but how
dare you put it so bluntly.

I thought you said it wasn't in Haruhi's nature
to be persuaded by words alone?
Well, certainly you have a point…
Mikuru, what do you think?
Huh? M-me?

Hmm… I guess so… It could be like that, I
think…

No no, now's the time to be more assertive
please, Asahina.

Now that you mention it, they've been pulling
all-nighters here for a while, right?
What about it?

Maybe they started having weird
hallucinations due to lack of sleep?

Humans instinctively try to escape from
painful or difficult things.

Seeing things or hearing things are prime
examples of that, don't you think?

A "phantom classroom” sounds perfectly
emblematic of escaping from reality to me.
Hmm…
Looks like she's not quite buying it.

Say, Nagato. Don't you think that kind of
hallucination is fairly normal?

Ugh, was handing it over to Nagato a
mistake?

Staring at monitors for extended time periods
causes strain on the eyeball and optic nerve.

Th-that's right. Exactly. Those guys have
been on computers the whole time, right?

With all these factors in mind, the misunder-
standing theory makes a lot of sense, right?

With Nagato's great assist coming out of left
field, I pressed for Haruhi's verdict.
Ugh… I guess. That could be right.
Phew…

It's a pretty poor explanation, but she seems
to be somewhat convinced.

For goodness' sake, hallucinating from
tiredness? I've had enough of false alarms!

I'd better barge in on the computer society
and have a go at them.

If you really want to pour salt on their tired
wounds, I can't stop you.

Why don't you do it when they're in a better
condition though?

What are you talking about? Striking your
enemy when they're weak is basic strategy!

My apologies, computer society. I hope you
don't mind taking one for world peace here.
You look rather tired.
Because I am rather tired.

I need to find the right timing to put an end
to this summer camp…

Looks like this is gonna be an unforgettable
summer—in both good and bad ways.
About Haruhi
